classification.difficultyReason: Use the sign of the velocity found in part (a) to establish motion in one direction over the first two seconds, then take the difference of the endpoint positions in the correct order.

content.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line so that the function $x(t)=(6-t)^3$ gives the particle’s position in metres at any time $t$ seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the particle’s velocity-time equation, and describe the significance of the sign.

answer.short: $v(t)=-3(6-t)^2$ m/s. The particle moves in the negative direction except at $t=6$ s, when its velocity is zero.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}v(t)&=x'(t)\\v(t)&=3(6-t)^2(-1)\\v(t)&=-3(6-t)^2\quad\text{m/s}\end{align*}$$ The square is positive for $t\ne6$, so the velocity is negative and the particle moves in the negative direction. At $t=6$ s the velocity is zero.

children.label: b
children.prompt: When and where is the velocity zero?

answer.short: At $t=6$ s, at the origin ($x=0$ m).
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}-3(6-t)^2&=0\\6-t&=0\\t&=6\end{align*}$$ At $t=6$ s, $x(6)=(6-6)^3=0$ m, so the particle is at the origin.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the particle’s initial position and velocity?

children.label: d
children.prompt: When is the particle at the origin?

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the distance travelled by the particle during the first 2 seconds.

answer.worked: The velocity is negative throughout the first 2 seconds, so the particle travels in one direction. $$\begin{align*}x(2)&=(6-2)^3\\x(2)&=64\quad\text{m}\\\text{Distance travelled}&=x(0)-x(2)\\\text{Distance travelled}&=216-64\\\text{Distance travelled}&=152\quad\text{m}\end{align*}$$
